etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French defensable, from Latin defensibilem. Equivalent to defense +‎ -ible.

definitions.definition: (of an installation, etc.) Capable of being defended against armed attack.

quote.citation: 1907, Ronald M. Burrows, The Discoveries In Crete, page 11:
quote.text: Not only were those cities fortified, but their architects based their whole system on the strategical possibilities of the site, and closely followed its defensible contours.

definitions.definition: (of an argument, etc.) Capable of being justified.
